questions.text:
Produce a piece of writing in te reo Māori (at least 150 words) on ONE of the following topics. Kuputaka/glossed vocabulary is provided to help but does not have to be included in your writing.

Topic 1: Whakatairitea ētahi hākinakina e rua. Whakamāramatia mai ko tēhea te mea pai ake.
Compare and contrast two sports. Explain which is better.
Kuputaka: kaha = strong; tere = fast; pārekareka = fun; uaua = difficult; hauora = health/fitness; rōpū = team

Topic 2: Matapakina mai tētahi raru i tō hapori. He aha ētahi rautaki hei whakaea i tēnei raru?
Discuss a problem in your community. What are some solutions?
Kuputaka: taiao = environment; para = rubbish; waka = transport; huarahi = road; hauora = health; rangatahi = young people

Topic 3: Tuhia mai tētahi kōrero mō tō rā tuatahi ki te kura hou. He aha ō kare ā-roto?
Write about your first day at a new school. What were your feelings?
Kuputaka: āwangawanga = worried; koa = happy; whakamā = shy; hoa = friend; kaiako = teacher; akomanga = classroom

Topic 4: Whakatairitea tō tino wāhi ki tētahi atu wāhi kāore e pai ki a koe. He aha ngā rerekētanga me ngā ōritenga?
Compare and contrast your favourite place with another place you don't like. What are the differences and similarities?
Kuputaka: ātaahua = beautiful; makariri = cold; wera = hot; ngahere = forest; moana = sea; tāone = town

Topic 5: Ko wai tō tino tangata i roto i tō whānau, ā, he aha te take he tino tangata ia ki a koe?
Who is the most important person in your whānau, and why are they so important to you?
Kuputaka: aroha = love; manaaki = to care for; tohutohu = to guide/advise; tautoko = to support; kaha = strong; māia = brave
questions.markingGuide:
This is a writing exam where you choose ONE topic and write at least 150 words in te reo Māori only.

Achieved (Paetae 3-4): Writes in te reo Māori on one of the topics. Writing is understandable and communication of ideas is mostly achieved. Shows sufficient basic evidence from Curriculum Levels 5 and 6. Contains errors but a few words in English for unknown translations are acceptable if infrequent. Simplistic ideas with few details or opinions.

Merit (Kaiaka 5-6): Writes in te reo Māori on one of the topics and adheres to the specific instructions. Writing is understandable with effective communication of ideas. Shows a range of complex evidence from Curriculum Levels 5 and 6. Contains few errors. Shows depth and regularly provides details and opinions.

Excellence (Kairangi 7-8): Comprehensive response in te reo Māori that shows a thorough understanding of the instructions. Communication of ideas is extensive. Shows a wide range of sophisticated evidence from Curriculum Levels 5 and 6. Contains minimal errors. Well-crafted response that is convincing; reasons and opinions are effectively placed and validate the candidate's ideas.
